Membership terms

The simple rules for ADD members and directory listings.

Draft: this is a starting template, not legal advice. Have a Nigerian lawyer review it, and fill in the bracketed details, before membership opens.

Last updated: November 2026

1. Tiers and fees

ADD has four tiers: Founding Patron, Studio Member, Maker / Emerging and Friend of ADD. Fees for each tier are published before you join, and you'll never be charged without agreeing first. Founding members who commit for 12 months get a founding rate.

2. Who can join

Practising creative businesses and makers in Nigeria across ADD's six pillars. Friends of ADD can be anyone who supports Nigerian design. We may ask for proof that a business is real and active, such as a CAC registration, professional registration or examples of completed work.

3. Your listing and content

You confirm that you own, or have permission to use, every image and piece of text you send us, and that photographers are credited where required. You give us permission to show that content on this website, on the Open Studios map and on ADD's social media to promote you. You can ask us to remove it at any time.

4. Accuracy

Keep your details up to date and tell us if anything changes. We may edit listings for length, clarity and consistency.

5. Enquiries and sales

Clients contact members directly. Any agreement you make with a client is between you and them. Sales made through ADD exhibitions and Pop-up Showrooms may carry a commission, which will always be agreed in writing before the event.

6. Fairness and conflicts of interest

ADD is a shared platform. Where a founder's or board member's own business is a member, this is declared openly. Programmes are balanced across the pillars.

7. Leaving or removal

You can leave at any time by emailing us. We may remove members whose listings are inaccurate or inactive, or who receive credible complaints of misconduct.

8. Changes

We may update these terms and will tell members by email when we do.

ADDAbuja Design District

ADD brings together fashion, architecture, interiors, art and product design to showcase Nigerian creativity, support collaboration and connect creative businesses with opportunities.
